data.narrative: The student chose asynchronous BullMQ analytics to keep redirects fast and explained the retry, idempotency, fallback, and backlog tradeoffs. Evidence covers redirect and analytics behavior, privacy, duplicate prevention, retention cleanup, and passing tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Connected async processing to redirect latency and identified the queue and worker tradeoff.
dimension_scores.evidence: Chose BullMQ because it keeps the redirect response fast while click events are processed by a background worker.

dimension_scores.observation: Used repeatable tests to verify event processing and duplicate handling.
dimension_scores.evidence: Module 7 regression evidence records duplicate eventId rejection and passing unit and E2E tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Preserved click-event privacy and protected analytics access.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verification confirms IP hashes are stored instead of raw IPs and analytics are owner-protected.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified queue failure and backlog risks with practical mitigations.
dimension_scores.evidence: Named retries, idempotency, durable fallback, monitoring, backlog alerts, and retention limits.

dimension_scores.observation: Explained the architecture choice and its operational risk clearly.
dimension_scores.evidence: Provided concise reasons for async processing and specific queue and worker failure mitigations.

strengths: Connects asynchronous processing to redirect latency and explains why retries need idempotency.
Supports implementation claims with concrete analytics, privacy, retention, and test evidence.
growth_areas: Define a firm capacity and backpressure policy for the durable fallback during a prolonged queue outage.
data.recommendation: Set an explicit outbox capacity threshold and the alert or backpressure action to take when it is reached.

public_evidence.artifact: BullMQ click analytics and protected analytics endpoint
public_evidence.student_action: Implemented and verified asynchronous click recording and time-window analytics.
public_evidence.technical_detail: BullMQ producer and worker with an owner-scoped analytics endpoint.
public_evidence.proof: Two redirects returned HTTP 302 and protected analytics counted two clicks; 10 unit and 48 E2E tests passed. See progress/evidence/module-07/build/click-analytics-verification.txt.
public_evidence.ability: Designs and verifies asynchronous analytics flows.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the ability to keep a high-traffic redirect path responsive while processing analytics separately.

public_evidence.student_action: Added and verified unique event IDs so retries do not double-count clicks.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Unique event_id constraint and duplicate-job handling in the worker.
public_evidence.proof: Regression evidence records duplicate eventId rejection and idempotent worker handling. See progress/evidence/module-07/fix/regression-summary.txt.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates protection against duplicate work in at-least-once job delivery.

public_evidence.student_action: Selected 30-day retention and verified purging of expired click events.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Retention purge removes click events beyond the configured retention window.
public_evidence.proof: The verification output records a 30-day cutoff and successful deletion of an expired event. See progress/evidence/module-07/build/click-analytics-verification.txt.
public_evidence.ability: Balances analytics usefulness with bounded data retention.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows attention to storage growth and operational maintenance.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Explained that retries reuse a unique eventId and a database UNIQUE constraint prevents duplicate click records.
Explained that analytics failures should not block the redirect.
Explained that a BullMQ worker processes analytics separately to keep redirects fast.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used duplicate delivery of a click event to connect eventId uniqueness with idempotent processing.
